title: Investigate the data_quality_checks runtime regression (+43% vs baseline)
description: task-012_5's retest measured data_quality_checks at 242 s avg against a 169 s baseline, with all four post-optimization observations (292/217/217, plus 231 at the 14:08 preliminary) above the 206 s baseline maximum and no overlap between the ranges. It is the only per-activity finding in the retest that clears a non-overlap test, and it now accounts for 21% of pipeline runtime against 17% at baseline. Causation is NOT established: task-012_3 never modified this notebook, so attributing it to V-Order or the broadcast hints is unfounded. The leading hypothesis is that gold_quality_history accumulates rows on every pipeline run — it is referenced 26 times in data_quality_checks — so if any check scans it unbounded, runtime grows monotonically with the number of runs ever executed. That would make this a design characteristic surfacing as an apparent regression rather than damage from the optimization work, and it would get worse indefinitely once task-010 puts the pipeline on a schedule.
acceptanceCriteria: The gold_quality_history read pattern in data_quality_checks is characterised statically first — every read is identified and classified as bounded (filtered to a run or window) or unbounded (whole-table scan). This half needs no Fabric access and should be done before anything is run.

The hypothesis is tested against data, not just inspection: gold_quality_history row count is recorded alongside the activity duration, so growth-vs-runtime can be correlated across the runs already measured in performance_optimized.md.
The conclusion states plainly whether accumulated history explains the regression, and if it does not, says so and leaves the cause open rather than substituting a second guess.

If unbounded scans are confirmed as the cause, the fix bounds the scan window rather than truncating history — the trend data is the point of the table (three quality-observability tables track quality over time per the data_quality_architecture doc).
The finding is written back into performance_optimized.md's regression section, which currently records the hypothesis as untested.

EVIDENCE: performance_optimized.md § What got worse (regressions) item 1, and the per-run tables for Runs 1-3. Baseline 120/180/206 s (the 206 is the one exact baseline figure; runs 1-2 were gap-derived), retest 292/217/217 s, preliminary 231 s.

WHY owner=both AND why Claude can act first (so this is correctly Pending, not Blocked): AC1 is pure static analysis of a notebook already in the repo — no Fabric access needed. Only AC2's row count requires Erik to run a query. This is the opposite of the FB-100 shape, where a both-owned task with an empty files_affected cannot start until the human acts.

DO NOT assume the optimization caused this. task-012_3 changed silver-to-gold (V-Order, broadcast hints, caching) and bronze-to-silver (caching); it did not touch data_quality_checks. A confident-sounding causal story here would be exactly the kind of unfounded attribution the retest write-up deliberately avoided.
URGENCY LINK: task-010 (pipeline scheduling) makes this worse if the hypothesis holds — a daily scheduled run adds history every day, so an unbounded scan degrades without bound.
